name: Arnoldi Krylov basis construction
definition: Start with unit q₁. For j=1,…,m form w=Aq_j, h_ij=q_i* w and w←w−h_ij q_i successively for i≤j; h_(j+1,j)=||w||₂, q_(j+1)=w/h_(j+1,j) if nonzero. In exact arithmetic A Q_m=Q_(m+1) H̄_m.
variables: A square real or complex matrix; * adjoint; q_i orthonormal basis vectors; H̄ upper Hessenberg projection with one extra row
assumptions: Nonzero initial vector, consistent inner product; stop at exact invariant-subspace breakdown or use a documented finite-precision policy.
limitations: Growing basis storage and loss of orthogonality; Ritz values are approximations, not necessarily certified eigenvalues.
failure_conditions: Near-zero residual or loss of orthogonality without safeguard
computation: Modified Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization of matrix-vector products; use reorthogonalization as needed.

source.citation: Bindel, D. (2025), Cornell CS 6210, Lanczos and Arnoldi, 17 November, Arnoldi section. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6210/2025fa/lec/2025-11-17.html

application: Construct a reduced subspace for a general numerical matrix analysis.
required_inputs: Square matrix or linear operator, initial vector, dimension limit and breakdown policy.
incompatible_methods: Ignoring breakdown or treating projected spectrum as exact

name: Symmetric Lanczos three-term recurrence
definition: For real symmetric A, q₀=0, β₀=0 and unit q₁, form w=Aq_j−β_(j−1)q_(j−1), α_j=q_jᵀw, w←w−α_j q_j, β_j=||w||₂, q_(j+1)=w/β_j when β_j>0.
variables: A symmetric matrix; q_j basis vectors; α_j and β_j tridiagonal coefficients
assumptions: Symmetry, unit initial vector, exact-arithmetic orthogonality; finite precision requires a monitored reorthogonalization or restart policy.
limitations: Loss of orthogonality can cause repeated spurious Ritz values; stop safely on breakdown.
failure_conditions: Nonsymmetric operator or unhandled near-zero β_j
computation: Apply matrix-vector products and three-term updates; use the resulting tridiagonal projection for numerical analysis.

source.citation: Bindel, D. (2026), Cornell CS 4220, Krylov subspace iterations, 16 March, three-term recurrence. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4220/2026sp/lec/2026-03-16.html

application: Build a compact projection of a symmetric numerical operator.
required_inputs: Symmetric matrix or operator, starting vector, stopping and orthogonality policy.
incompatible_methods: Applying the symmetric recurrence to an arbitrary nonsymmetric matrix
mechanism_note: Symmetric specialization of Arnoldi; three-term recurrence materially changes computational storage and operations, not independent mathematical evidence.

name: Unshifted QR eigenvalue iteration
definition: Factor A_k=Q_k R_k with orthogonal Q_k and triangular R_k; set A_(k+1)=R_k Q_k=Q_kᵀ A_k Q_k.
variables: A_k real square matrix; Q_k orthogonal factor; R_k triangular factor
assumptions: Consistent QR factorization; convergence to diagonal form for real symmetric matrices requires appropriate spectral and initialization conditions; repeated or opposite equal magnitudes may stall.
limitations: Unshifted convergence can be slow or fail to separate equal-magnitude eigenvalues; not a complete modern eigensolver.
failure_conditions: Assuming convergence for arbitrary matrices or using a nonorthogonal factorization
computation: Repeated orthogonal QR factorizations and similarity updates, monitor off-diagonal residual and iteration limit.

source.citation: Bindel, D. (2026), Cornell CS 4220, From power methods to QR iteration, 6 March. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4220/2026sp/lec/2026-03-06.html

application: General numerical study of orthogonal eigenvalue iteration.
required_inputs: Square matrix, QR implementation, convergence criterion and iteration bound.
incompatible_methods: Treating unconverged diagonal entries as certified eigenvalues

name: Givens-rotation QR elimination
definition: For a,b not both zero let r=√(a²+b²), c=a/r, s=b/r; G=[[c,s],[−s,c]] maps (a,b)ᵀ to (r,0)ᵀ. Apply embedded rotations to eliminate subdiagonal matrix entries.
variables: a,b entries to rotate; c,s cosine and sine; G orthogonal plane rotation
assumptions: Finite real matrix, stable hypotenuse computation, identity or declared sign convention for zero pair.
limitations: Dense matrices often favor Householder transformations; repeated updates require stable numerical implementation.
failure_conditions: Overflow in naive norm or division by zero
computation: Use stable hypotenuse, apply rotations in elimination order, and accumulate the orthogonal factor if required.

source.citation: Bindel, D. (2026), Cornell CS 4220, Least squares and QR, 23 February, Givens rotations section. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4220/2026sp/lec/2026-02-23.html

application: General sparse or incremental numerical factorization.
required_inputs: Real matrix and a stable plane-rotation routine.
incompatible_methods: Using unstable squared sums for extreme entries
mechanism_note: Local plane-rotation elimination instead of full-column reflections.

name: Modified Gram–Schmidt QR factorization
definition: For columns a_j set v_j=a_j. For i=1,…,n set r_ii=||v_i||₂, q_i=v_i/r_ii; for j>i set r_ij=q_iᵀv_j, v_j←v_j−r_ij q_i.
variables: a_j input columns; v_j residuals; q_i orthonormal columns; R upper triangular
assumptions: Real full-column-rank matrix; positive residual norms; finite-precision orthogonality monitored.
limitations: Loss of orthogonality on ill-conditioned matrices; not rank-revealing by itself.
failure_conditions: Zero or near-zero residual norm without rank handling
computation: Successively project remaining columns onto each newly normalized basis vector.

source.citation: Zhang, Z. (2023), QR and least square, 17 March, p. 2, Algorithm 2. https://www.math.cmu.edu/~zechengz/spring_2023_nla/0317.pdf

application: General orthonormal basis construction for numerical linear algebra.
required_inputs: Full-column-rank real matrix and numerical breakdown threshold.
